To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tissue staining of carcino-embryonic antigen in colorectal carcinomas can be substituted for the preoperative serum level of carcinoembryo-nyonic antigen, and that both parameters can be used to predict survival in patients with Dukes' stage c disease.

tissue staining can substitute for preoperative serum level, that tissue stain and elevated serum level identify poor prognosis patients in Dukes' stages C and D, and that tissue stain and serum levels do not identify patients with greater risk than either procedure alone.

tissue staining with CEA is a good substitute for preoperative serum level determination, that the combination of tissue staining and elevated serum level is not superior to either test alone, and that both tests are useful only in Dukes' stages C and D.
